ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a rectangle, and the midpoints of the left and right sides are labeled M and N respectively; MN is a horizontal line passing through the middle of the rectangle. Inside the rectangle there is a polyline, starting from the lower left corner, successively reaching a point on the top side, a point on the bottom side, a point on the top side, and finally reaching the lower right corner. The gray shaded regions are distributed in several triangular regions between this polyline and the middle horizontal line MN. Then reason: Let the width of the rectangle be W and the height be H. Because M and N are the midpoints of the left and right sides, MN is the horizontal midline at height H/2. According to the x-coordinates of adjacent vertices of the polyline, divide the rectangle into several vertical strips. Within each vertical strip, one segment of the polyline is from the bottom side to the top side, or from the top side to the bottom side, so its intersection with the midline MN is at the exact middle position of the width of that vertical strip. If the width of a certain vertical strip is d, then the shading inside that strip is composed of two congruent right triangles; the vertical height of each triangle is H/2, and the horizontal base is d/2, so the total area of the two triangles is 2 × (1/2 × H/2 × d/2) = dH/4. Adding all the vertical strips together, the sum of all d is exactly the total width W of the rectangle, so the total shaded area is WH/4. The total area of the rectangle is WH, so the fraction occupied by the shaded area is (WH/4)/(WH) = 1/4.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a rectangle cut by the horizontal segment MN, with M and N on the left and right sides, and a zigzag broken line running from the lower-left corner to an upper point, then to a lower point, then to an upper point, then to the lower-right corner. Let the rectangle have width W and height H. Use the text fact that M and N are midpoints, so MN is the horizontal midline at height H/2. Divide the rectangle into vertical strips using the x-coordinates of each consecutive pair of zigzag vertices. In each strip, the slanted segment runs from the bottom side to the top side or from the top side to the bottom side, so it crosses the midline halfway across the strip. The shaded part in that strip consists of two congruent right triangles, each with vertical height H/2 and horizontal width half the strip width. Thus the shaded area in a strip of width d is dH/4. Summing over all strips gives H/4 times the total strip widths, i.e. WH/4, so the shaded fraction is 1/4.
